documents.title: Client readiness email
documents.summary: Unstructured request with client facts, timing and an unsupported reporting promise.
content: New mandate won - Alpenridge Pension Foundation - USD 250m

Team, Alpenridge has selected us for a new institutional separate account. The client is a Swiss pension foundation based in Zurich. Please target funding on 23 November 2026. The opportunity is marked Closed Won.

The global investment-grade fixed-income mandate is USD 250 million equivalent, with USD 50 million cash and USD 200 million of existing bonds. The reporting currency is CHF; the operational funding reference is USD equivalent. Please do not infer a currency conversion or hedge ratio from these figures.

The client wants a weekly CHF performance, attribution and ESG pack by Monday 08:00 Zurich time. In the sales discussion we said this should be achievable. The draft investment guidelines prohibit tobacco above 5% revenue and ask for no thermal-coal exposure.

FX forwards and interest-rate futures are requested from launch. Custody is with fictional Alpine Custody Services AG. Attached: opportunity brief, approval register, draft IMA, client policy, capability note and indicative transfer file.

CORG approval is referenced in the register. Please check the final IO review and conditions before initiating the formal request. We need one coordinated response to the client, not seven separate chasers.
Paragraphs 2-4 establish funding, reporting and restriction requests. This email is a request, not evidence that reporting support or approvals exist.

documents.title: Investment management agreement - draft v3
documents.summary: Unsigned contract language contains a threshold mismatch and ambiguous coal restriction.
content: DRAFT - NOT EXECUTED. Illustrative extracts between Alpenridge Pension Foundation and a Capital Group contracting entity to be confirmed by Legal. No signatures, legal addresses, or actual account instructions are supplied.

The proposed discretionary mandate is global investment-grade fixed income with an initial USD 250,000,000 equivalent portfolio. Assets may be delivered as cash and agreed eligible securities. Planned launch: 23 November 2026, subject to operational readiness.
3.1 Maximum corporate issuer exposure: 5% of total account NAV at issuer-parent level; sovereign securities are excluded from this corporate-issuer test. Missing issuer mapping requires review.

3.2 No below-investment-grade purchases under the agreed rating methodology. Downgrades, missing ratings, reconciliation differences and passive breaches follow the approved exception process. Duration and currency controls require final manager approval and system validation.
4.1 The Manager shall not purchase securities of companies deriving more than 5% of revenue from tobacco production. The Account shall have no exposure to thermal coal.
4.2 Client exclusions shall be translated into system rules only after Legal and FI PC agree the measurement scope, threshold, provider, parent mapping, missing-data treatment and effective date.

Clause 4.1 is intentionally incomplete. The phrase "more than 5%" conflicts with the policy in D05 at exactly 5%. "No exposure to thermal coal" does not specify extraction, generation, revenue threshold, subsidiaries or indirect exposure.

5.1 FX forwards may hedge currency exposure and interest-rate futures may manage duration, subject to finalized permitted instruments, counterparty documentation, relevant market access and operational controls. Inclusion in an IMA does not establish trading readiness.

Annual rates on the stated USD-equivalent fee basis: 0.18% on the first USD 100 million and 0.14% on assets above USD 100 million up to USD 250 million. Quarterly in arrears. Fee currency, valuation convention, proration and tax treatment remain for Legal/Billing agreement.

Illustrative annual fee at a constant USD 250m: USD 180,000 + USD 210,000 = USD 390,000. A simple quarter is USD 97,500 before proration or adjustments. This is a synthetic arithmetic example, not Capital Group pricing.

Weekly CHF performance, attribution and ESG reporting by Monday 08:00 Zurich time is requested. Until the service schedule is finalized, this is an unresolved request, not an accepted service commitment.

Client signature: not provided. Manager signature: not provided. Tax and AML evidence are reviewed through the appropriate specialist workstreams. No funding or trade release is authorized by this draft.

documents.title: Indicative custody and transfer file
documents.summary: Twelve holdings total USD 200m; two exclusions and one unknown create a USD 30m transition decision.
content: Alpine Custody Services AG (fictional) | Account AC-DEMO-7712 | Report date 11 September 2026. Indicative holdings are USD-equivalent market values provided by the custodian for demo analysis; they are not face values or executable instructions.
Indicative in-kind total: USD 200m. Separate planned cash: USD 50m. Total mandate: USD 250m. Security identifiers are deliberately nontradeable demo IDs.

The custodian can provisionally support 23 November subject to final eligible-securities list, confirmed market access, reconciled account details, signed instructions and independently verified settlement details. No bank routing numbers, account credentials or wire instructions are included.

Corporate issuer exposure is measured against total USD 250m account NAV, not just the USD 200m transfer file. Each USD 10m corporate parent position is 4%; government rows are exempt only from the corporate-issuer concentration cap.

ESG measures are synthetic percentages of issuer revenue. Missing values must remain unknown. Dataset timestamp is 11 September; refresh is required before funding. A September screen is not valid proof of November readiness.
Testable seeded outcomes after D09 clarification

Alder Tobacco Holdings at exactly 5% fails the agreed >=5% tobacco rule. Granite Basin Mining at 12% fails the agreed >=10% thermal-coal extraction rule. Meridian Industrials has missing ESG data and goes to review; it is not automatically compliant.

Illustrative transition choice: retain these three USD 10m positions with the outgoing manager and replace USD 30m of in-kind funding with cash. Proposed revised mix is USD 170m in-kind + USD 80m cash. This is a planning proposal, not an order to sell or transfer.

documents.title: Comparable onboarding casebook
documents.summary: Three reasoned analogues support a tailored playbook without copying prior approvals.
content: Retrieval fixtures - all three cases are fictional
History informs recommendations; no retrieved case grants authority or proves current system capability. Similarity is explained through shared attributes, not a fabricated success probability.

H01 - Alpinecrest Foundation
Switzerland / IG bonds / CHF reporting

Weekly attribution was requested; client accepted weekly holdings plus a monthly validated pack. Match: domicile, asset class, reporting currency. Limitation: different deadlines and provider dependencies.

H02 - Northbridge Endowment
Global bonds / tobacco restriction

IMA said >5%; client policy said >=5%. Legal clarified the boundary and FI PC tested values below, at and above 5%. Match: contractual ambiguity. Limitation: US endowment context; not evidence of Swiss law.

H03 - Seabrook Insurance
In-kind bonds / derivatives

Counterparty setup threatened launch. Team agreed a cash substitution for restricted securities and deferred derivatives until approvals were complete. Match: transition and readiness dependencies. Limitation: insurance mandate controls differ.

Borrow the decision pattern, not the prior conclusion. Open a reporting-service decision, obtain client/Legal clarification of restriction thresholds, test the transfer file, and require the derivatives setup owner to confirm feasibility.
Access controls, case-level permissions and permission-aware retrieval would be required before real historical records are used.

documents.title: Client restriction clarification
documents.summary: Resolves thresholds and scope; still requires Legal and FI PC approval.
content: Client RM and Legal / 15 September 2026, 10:10 UTC

For the contractual schedule, tobacco production is excluded at greater than or equal to 5% of total issuer revenue. For thermal coal, we mean extraction revenue greater than or equal to 10%; we are not requesting a separate coal-power generation threshold in this schedule.

Apply the tests to directly held corporate securities using the approved issuer-parent mapping and Demo ESG Dataset version 2026-09. Indirect fund exposure is outside this draft rule and would require a separate decision. Missing, unmapped or stale observations require review before purchase or transfer; do not assume zero exposure.

Data must be refreshed for go-live. For this synthetic scenario, the agreed freshness threshold is 30 calendar days at screening. Actual thresholds and licensed providers must be agreed by the appropriate teams.

Please prepare the revised schedule for our approval. This email clarifies intent but does not execute the IMA. Legal owns contractual language; FI PC owns the rule interpretation and approves implementation after boundary testing.

No purchase or transfer of a direct corporate security where tobacco-production revenue is >=5% or thermal-coal extraction revenue is >=10%, measured at the approved issuer-parent level. Missing, unmapped or >30-day-old data requires manual review and blocks release pending disposition.

documents.title: Late client change request
documents.summary: Replans the critical path and invalidates affected prior approvals.
content: Can we bring funding forward to 9 November?

Our board would like to move launch from 23 November to 9 November 2026, two weeks earlier. Can we still start with FX forwards and interest-rate futures? Please preserve the revised reporting service and exclusions.

The setup owner estimates derivatives readiness on 16 November. Custody and core cash-bond setup could support 9 November, but only if the relevant teams and client approve a bonds-only launch and the revised hedge/duration implications. These are scenario estimates, not commitments.

A. Preserve the full mandate on 23 November; re-confirm client date preference. B. Explore 9 November with derivatives deferred; reopen Legal/PM, FI PC, transition, custody and Operations decisions. C. Retain the current plan while seeking an evidence-backed acceleration of derivatives readiness; do not invent an earlier completion date.

For the guided demo choose B. Record client and accountable owner acceptance of the staged mandate; rerun screening and funding controls for the new date. No previous funding approval may carry forward automatically.

CUS-193: core bond markets open; custody details independently verified by maker/checker; no payment information shown.
RUL-981: Legal/FI PC-approved rules tested in a sandbox; current ESG and issuer mapping snapshot 6 Nov; initial funding portfolio passes approved tests.

TRN-661: nine eligible positions USD 170m plus USD 80m cash; reconciliation complete; client/transition/PM acceptance recorded.
REP-117 and BILL-051: sample report accepted, service calendar configured, fee tier test and currency/proration setup accepted.

GCS maker recommends ready. An independent Operations checker must record the final simulated funding-release decision against the current plan. AI cannot attest that signatures, reviews, custody verification or approvals occurred.
This second page is an event fixture used only after simulated release. FND-DEMO-119 records USD 80m cash and USD 170m in-kind received and reconciled. No transfer is initiated by the demo.
USD 250m total received; nine securities plus cash reconcile.
Current dataset re-screened; no unresolved tobacco/coal flags in accepted assets. Other mandate controls remain governed by approved monitoring.
Trading disabled; follow-up readiness review on/after 16 Nov, no automatic activation.
First weekly holdings report scheduled 10 Nov; first monthly pack scheduled using configured business-day calendar.
Fee basis and benchmark mapped; first-cycle service review assigned.
No unresolved blocking demo exception; monitoring owners retained.
The demo records these as imported synthetic events. It does not connect to a custodian, create a production account, verify actual AML documents or execute a trade.

risks.action: Import final governance closure, then let Operations initiate.

risks.title: Weekly report promise exceeds capability
risks.why: Monday 08:00 weekly CHF attribution conflicts with the documented reconciliation cycle.
risks.action: Agree Tuesday holdings + monthly validated attribution with the client.

risks.title: Restriction language changes the result
risks.why: At exactly 5% tobacco revenue, >5% and >=5% produce different eligibility; coal scope is undefined.
risks.action: Obtain clarification, approve contract language and test rules.

risks.why: Two excluded positions and one unknown-data position cannot be treated as eligible in-kind funding.
